policy.title_zh: 公費流感及新冠疫苗接種踴躍 請符合資格民眾儘速接種 及早獲得保護力
policy.title_en: Public flu and COVID vaccinations strong; eligible people urged to get vaccinated soon for early protection
policy.summary: The CDC reports strong uptake of public flu and COVID vaccines, notes ongoing flu activity and severe cases, and urges eligible people to vaccinate early before the holiday travel period.
policy.why: CDC links ongoing severe flu activity to unvaccinated older adults and urges pre-holiday vaccination, framing the current severity narrative.

policy.title_zh: 「左流右新 護肺顧心」10月1日公費流感及新冠疫苗同步開打
policy.title_en: 'Left flu, right COVID, protect lungs and heart': public flu and COVID vaccines open together Oct 1
policy.summary: The Taiwan CDC press release reports the October 1 launch of public flu and COVID vaccines and urges eligible people to get both, with the minister and officials receiving shots at the event.
policy.why: Launch event confirmed 7.05 million flu doses procured including enhanced vaccine, the figure now used to judge supply adequacy.

policy.title_zh: 2026年度公費流感及新冠疫苗第一階段將於10月1日開打 接種左流右新疫苗還可獲得1350健康幣
policy.title_en: 2026 publicly funded flu and COVID-19 vaccine first stage opens October 1; receiving Left flu, right new vaccines earns 1350 health coins
policy.summary: The CDC announces the first stage of publicly funded flu and COVID-19 vaccination starts October 1 for 11 groups, with a second stage from November 2, and urges eligible people to get vaccinated; standard and enhanced flu vaccine quantities and priority for enhanced vaccine in long-term care facilities are described.
policy.why: Sets the 2026 programme baseline: phase 1 for 11 groups from October 1 with about 6.449 million standard and 170,000 enhanced doses plus health-coin incentives.

policy.title_zh: 流感及新冠於仍處流行期且流感疫情持續上升 呼籲民眾連假期間加強自主防疫 出現重症危險徵兆儘速就醫

policy.summary: Taiwan CDC reports flu activity slightly rising and still epidemic, with 165 new severe cases and 30 deaths last week, and notes 67.8% of severe cases did not get this season's flu vaccine.

policy.summary: Taiwan CDC says flu is rising in epidemic period, urges protective measures and notes most severe cases were unvaccinated.

policy.summary: The CDC says flu has entered its epidemic period, reports severe cases and deaths, and notes 68.6% of severe cases had not received this season's flu vaccine.

policy.title_zh: 流感及新冠疫情持續 呼籲民眾留意個人衛生習慣 出現重症危險徵兆應儘速就醫治療
policy.title_en: Flu and COVID continue; public urged to practise hygiene and seek prompt care for severe warning signs
policy.summary: The CDC reports rising flu and COVID risk at school start, with 69.4% of severe flu cases this season unvaccinated, and urges hygiene and prompt care.

policy.title_zh: 因應各級學校即將開學，疾管署呼籲學校與家長落實衛生防護，防範腸病毒、新冠、流感及登革熱疫情
policy.title_en: CDC urges schools and parents to take hygiene measures against enterovirus, COVID, flu and dengue as schools reopen
policy.summary: Taiwan CDC urges schools and parents to practise hygiene as schools reopen, reporting current COVID and flu activity and asking eligible people to get COVID vaccination.

policy.summary: The Taiwan CDC notifies clinicians that subsidised flu antiviral eligibility is expanded from 24 August to 30 September due to rising influenza-like illness visits.

policy.title_zh: 國內外近期流感疫情緩升，疾管署自今年8月24日起至9月30日擴大公費流感抗病毒藥劑使用條件

policy.summary: The Taiwan CDC announces expanded eligibility for subsidised flu antivirals from 24 August to 30 September as influenza-like illness visits rise slightly.

policy.title_zh: 國內流感疫情雖尚未進入流行期，但已有緩升趨勢，以A型流感為主

entries.headline: Weekly flu toll hits five-year high: 219 severe cases, 44 deaths
entries.why: Multiple outlets carried the record severity figures over three days, and doctors tied them to vaccination appeals for older and chronically ill people. This is now the dominant frame for all flu coverage.

entries.headline: Public flu uptake reaches 1.91 million in eight days; official voices supply worry
entries.why: Reports quote Lo Yi-chun worrying that supply may not be enough, against 7.05 million doses procured. Supply adequacy is likely to become a political and media question if demand holds.

entries.headline: Taiwan CDC: uptake strong, severe cases mostly unvaccinated older adults
entries.zh: 公費流感及新冠疫苗接種踴躍 請符合資格民眾儘速接種 及早獲得保護力
entries.why: The CDC's latest notice frames severity around unvaccinated older adults and urges vaccination before holiday travel. This sets the official message that local bureaus and doctors are amplifying.

entries.headline: Posts report self-pay flu stock delays to November and NT$1,950 prices
entries.why: Users report Kaohsiung clinics without self-pay stock until November and complain about cost, while others report limited brand choice for public doses. Thin but high-engagement signal of access friction outside the public programme.

entries.headline: Paediatric flu dosing rule change and nasal-spray fever posts confuse parents
entries.why: Media report children 6 months to 3 years now need two doses this year, and parents post conflicting clinic answers and fever worries about nasal spray. Clarity on paediatric schedules is an emerging issue.

entries.headline: Clinic post promotes adjuvanted flu vaccine with unverified comparative protection claims
entries.why: A clinic's Threads post claims 20-30% better protection and 12-month duration and invites bookings; it is flagged as misleading. Comparative claims around enhanced vaccines are a compliance and reputational sensitivity.

watch.text: Planned start of 150,000 Novavax COVID doses alongside the joint flu and COVID programme.
Whether self-pay flu stock arrives at clinics as posts report, and whether flu activity eases as media forecast.
Whether severe-case and death counts stay at five-year highs and whether officials repeat supply concerns.

qa.q: Is there an official flu vaccine shortage?
qa.a: No official shortage notice in the digest. CDC procured 7.05 million doses (about 6.449 million standard and 170,000 enhanced); 1.91 million were given in eight days and an official said supply may not suffice. Social posts report self-pay stock delays in Kaohsiung.

Low-level only. A side-effect diary post and parents' nasal-spray fever posts drew engagement, PTS reported a first vaccine relief award for leg paralysis, and two low-engagement posts making misleading safety claims were flagged. Mainstream media coverage remains pro-vaccination.

qa.q: Anything on RSV, Tdap or high-dose flu?
qa.a: Very little. RSV volume rose from 0 to 7 items, led by a Threads post summarising a European maternal RSV vaccine study; Tdap had 5 items, mainly via chronic lung disease recommendations; high-dose flu had zero items. Enhanced-type coverage fell from 18 to 12.

narratives.title: Public flu and COVID programme uptake surge
narratives.para: Media and officials report record early uptake of the 1 October public flu and COVID programme, with cumulative figures passing 1.9 million flu doses in eight days and local bureaus adding holiday sites.

narratives.title: Health coin incentives and local rewards
narratives.para: Coverage credits the health coin reward and local prize schemes with boosting uptake, while some note older adults struggle with the digital access needed to claim them.

narratives.title: Supply strain, stock-outs and self-pay access
narratives.para: An official's worry about sufficiency is echoed by posts reporting limited brands at clinics, self-pay stock not arriving until November and price complaints.

narratives.title: Chronic disease and cardiovascular risk framing
narratives.para: Doctors and media link vaccination to protection for people with kidney disease, diabetes, lung disease and cardiovascular risk, with some coverage naming RSV and pertussis vaccines for COPD and asthma patients.

narratives.title: Side-effect experiences and safety doubts
narratives.para: High-engagement posts describe post-shot symptoms, a first vaccine injury relief payout drew coverage, and a few posts question co-administration and liability or claim vaccines harm elders.

narratives.title: Japan's early season and regional demand
narratives.para: Coverage of Japan's unusually early flu season and vaccine supply feeds Taiwanese interest in Japanese-made vaccines and demand at home.

narratives.title: Maternal RSV vaccination and infant protection
narratives.para: A single Threads post summarising a European study on maternal RSV vaccination and infant hospitalisation marks the start of thin RSV conversation.

misinfo.claim: Adjuvanted Japanese flu vaccine gives 20-30% more protection than standard vaccines and lasts 12 months
misinfo.note: Clinic promotional claim for a prescription vaccine; track spread and advertising-compliance angle, keep any company comment to approved label information, no amplification.

misinfo.claim: Vaccines contain viral particles and community calls to vaccinate over-65s endanger elders
misinfo.note: Single low-engagement post; monitor only, existing CDC and medical myth-busting content is sufficient.

misinfo.claim: Receiving flu and COVID shots together is untested and the campaign is electioneering
misinfo.note: Zero-engagement comment; monitor for co-administration safety and liability questions recurring as uptake grows.

voices.text: A post summarises a European pooled real-world study linking prenatal RSV vaccination to about 74% relative risk reduction in infant RSV hospitalisation, and notes the figure is relative and recommendations vary by country.
A post logs multi-day symptoms after a GSK flu vaccine, including fever, body aches, headache and fatigue.
A parent says several mothers reported fever after nasal spray flu vaccine and asks whether to choose an injection for their child instead.
A post says a self-paid flu vaccine cost NT$1,950 and complains about the expense.
A post claims that flu, measles, varicella, hepatitis B and HPV vaccines contain or use viruses and says a local office's call for seniors to get vaccinated endangers them.
A clinic promotes an adjuvanted flu vaccine, claiming 20 to 30 percent better protection and 12 months of coverage, and invites people to get it at its clinic.
